Y7 SCOPE
Y5 does not ask whether physics rescues this benchmark. Y3's requirement and Y4's
measured arm settle that on their own, and 80% of a number below the requirement is
still below it. Y5 asks whether a COMPUTED gain is as good as a MEASURED one,
because there is no ChIP for the overwhelming majority of the 612,133 edges.
Y8 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
One factor, one cell line, one perturbation. NR3C1 is the best case by construction
-- it is the drug's own receptor -- so a failure here bounds the others and a
success here does not generalise to factors whose ligand is not in the medium.
The computed arm uses a promoter window only. Loop 185 measured that distal
elements carry real signal, so a promoter-only occupancy is a floor for what
sequence-based binding could contribute.
Berg-von Hippel treats a PWM as an additive energy model. Real binding has
interdependence between positions, and loop 184 measured co-binding at 0.8455
against motif at 0.6228 -- most of what decides occupancy is not the site.
A set point is not a gain. This measures whether sequence predicts where a gene
ENDS UP, which is the product of all its gains, not any single edge weight.
